outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the unit-square upper bound moved to n^(-7/6+o(1)) (Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov, arXiv Sept 2024, Inventiones 2025); on 6 October 2026 OpenAI released a manuscript claiming a power improvement of the unit-square lower bound to n^(-2+eta), whose Lean statement is still sorry-marked in the repository I could read; and variant-container and finite-n record work (AlphaEvolve, Sudermann-Merx, community leaderboards, Blinov's conditional draft) accumulated through September and October 2026.
problem_asks: The statement asks for (1) improved LOWER bounds and (2) improved UPPER bounds on the asymptotic order of the optimal minimum triangle area for n points, i.e. the Heilbronn triangle quantity as n grows. The statement names no container. The Wikipedia article it links is about the unit square, so the working reading is: Delta(n) = the largest possible minimum triangle area over n points in the unit square, and its growth rate as n tends to infinity. Variant containers (unit disc, unit-area convex regions, equilateral or right triangles, the unit cube and higher dimensions, k-gons) are arguably 'the Heilbronn triangle problem' by name; under section 2.1 they are analogues, and each event below says which container it concerns. The statement does not ask for exact small-n values, though finite-n records are recorded as events because they bear on the same quantity.

events.what_happened: Komlos, Pintz and Szemeredi (1981): upper bound for the unit-square optimum of the form exp(c sqrt(log n)) / n^(8/7), extending Roth's density-increment method (as summarised by the Wikipedia article and the Erdos #507 page). The 1981 paper itself was not opened; known second-hand only.
events.delivers: Unit square: every n points contain a triangle of area at most about exp(c sqrt(log n)) / n^(8/7) (second-hand statement of the bound).
events.remains: Everything else; superseded by Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov 2023 and 2024.
events.direction: Upper bound on the optimum.

events.what_happened: Komlos, Pintz and Szemeredi (1982): lower bound Omega(log n / n^2) for the unit-square optimum, disproving Heilbronn's conjecture that the optimum is O(n^(-2)) by a logarithmic factor (as cited by the Wikipedia article and the Erdos #507 page). Original not opened.
events.delivers: Unit square: some configuration of n points has all triangles of area at least c log n / n^2 (second-hand statement). The Erdos #507 page records Erdos's own weaker lower bound of order 1/n^2.
events.remains: Any power-type improvement of the lower bound; the sharp order.
events.direction: Lower bound on the optimum; disproves the O(n^(-2)) conjecture by a log factor.

events.what_happened: Roth (1951): the first non-trivial upper bound, by a density-increment argument, extended from the unit square to closed convex regions of positive area. The Wikipedia article gives O(1/(n sqrt(log log n))); a search excerpt instead quotes 1/(n-2) as Roth's simple bound. The primary paper was not opened, so the exact form is unresolved.
events.delivers: Upper bound on the optimum for the unit square and convex regions (exact form unresolved, see what_happened).
events.remains: Superseded.
events.doubts: The exact form of Roth's bound differs between the Wikipedia article and a search excerpt; not resolved.
events.direction: Upper bound on the optimum.

events.what_happened: Comellas and Yebra (2002), 'New lower bounds for Heilbronn numbers', Electron. J. Combin. 9 (R6): simulated annealing with analytic refinement gives new unit-square lower bounds for n = 7 to 12; the authors state they have no optimality proof. Seen only in a search excerpt and as a citation in the Sudermann-Merx paper; not opened.
events.delivers: Finite-n lower bounds on the unit-square optimum for n = 7 to 12 (numerical configurations, not proved optimal).
events.remains: Asymptotics; optimality at these n.
events.directly_checkable: The configurations are listed in the paper; not examined.
events.direction: Lower bound at specific n.
events.object: Numerical configurations of 7 to 12 points in the unit square found by simulated annealing and refined to nearby local maxima. Not examined.

events.what_happened: Chen, Xu and Zeng (2017): branch-and-bound on CPU and GPU clusters certifies the unit-square n = 9 value, reported as 31 days of computation (cited by Monji, Modir and Kocuk and by the Wikipedia article). Not opened.
events.delivers: Finite-n: a computer-assisted bracket for the unit-square n = 9 optimum (second-hand).
events.remains: Asymptotics.
events.direction: Finite-n bound (bracket).

ai.disclosed_cost: About 31 days of cluster computing (as cited by Monji, Modir and Kocuk).

events.what_happened: Dehbi and Zeng (2022), 'Heilbronn's problem of eight points in the square', J. Systems Sci. Complexity: numerical search combined with symbolic computation for the unit-square n = 8 case (second-hand from the Wikipedia article and a search excerpt). Not opened.
events.delivers: Finite-n (n = 8) unit-square bound, computer-assisted.
events.remains: Asymptotics. Later square certifications for n <= 9 are in monji-2025 and sudermann-2026a.
events.direction: Finite-n bound.

events.what_happened: Zakharov, 'Upper bounds for Heilbronn's triangle problem in higher dimensions', arXiv:2211.15715 (v1 28 Nov 2022; v4 7 Jan 2024; Bull. London Math. Soc., DOI 10.1112/blms.13020). The abstract gives, for points in [0,1]^d: a simplex of d+1 points of volume at most C_d n^(-log d + 6); a set of 1.1d points with convex hull volume at most C_d n^(-1.1); and k >= 4 sqrt(d) points spanning a (k-1)-simplex of volume at most C_d n^(-(k-1)/d - k^2/(8d^2)). Exponents as transcribed by the fetch; not checked against the paper.
events.revisions: v1 28 Nov 2022; v2 6 Mar 2023; v3 25 Sep 2023; v4 7 Jan 2024 ('minor corrections and fixed computational mistakes').
events.delivers: Higher-dimensional cube variant only; says nothing about the unit square exponent, and is not a unit-square result.
events.remains: The unit-square problem and the planar exponent.

events.what_happened: Agama, arXiv:2006.05269, v1 (5 June 2020, titled 'An improved lower bound of the Heilbron triangle problem'): using the method of compression, claims a lower bound Delta(s) >> log^2(s) / s^2 for s points 'in the plane R^2'. The version list runs to v13 (6 May 2026); the domain and bound change in later versions (see agama-2024 and agama-2026).
events.revisions: v1 5 Jun 2020; v2 12 Jun 2020; v3 2 Dec 2020; v4 17 Jul 2021; v5 17 Aug 2021; v6-v8 Jan 2022; v9 16 Mar 2024; v10 8 Apr 2024; v11 19 Jun 2024; v12 8 Mar 2026; v13 6 May 2026. Only v1, v9, v10, v12 and v13 were opened.

events.doubts: The claimed bound and its domain change across versions: v1 gives log^2 s / s^2 for the plane; v9 to v13 give log s / (s sqrt s) for the unit disc. The arXiv comments field on v13 records an administrative note of substantial text overlap with arXiv:1912.08075 and arXiv:2002.00502. No peer-reviewed version and no expert engagement were found.

events.what_happened: Maldague, Wang and Zakharov, 'Heilbronn's triangle problem in three dimensions', arXiv:2510.26644 (30 Oct 2025, 34 pages, single version): any n points in the unit cube [0,1]^3 contain a triangle of area at most C n^(-2/3-c) for an absolute c > 0. The paper says the proof gives 'an explicit, albeit very tiny, value of c' and that 'one should be able to take c = 10^-100 or so' without optimisation. The proof uses a point-line theorem with exponent gamma that the paper calls 'extremely poor'. An AI-generated review (Moonlight) repeats the 10^-100 figure; the figure is in the paper itself.
events.delivers: Three-dimensional cube variant only: upper bound n^(-2/3-c), improving the trivial pigeonhole bound n^(-2/3). Not the unit square. The planar analogue is the Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov result.
events.remains: The unit square; the sharp three-dimensional exponent; dimension 4 and up (per the paper's remarks).

events.what_happened: Cohen, Pohoata and Zakharov, 'Lower bounds for incidences', arXiv:2409.07658 (v1 11 Sept 2024; v2 18 Mar 2025, 'to appear in Inventiones Mathematicae'). Gives a point-tube incidence bound and deduces that any n points in the unit square contain a triangle of area at most n^(-7/6+o(1)). Published as Invent. math. 240 (2025), 1045-1118, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01331-2; MIT DSpace gives an issue date of 14 Mar 2025 (search excerpt; not opened).
events.revisions: v1 11 Sep 2024; v2 18 Mar 2025 (revised, 116 KB, 53 pages).
events.delivers: Unit square, all large n: optimum at most n^(-7/6+o(1)). Per the abstract, this matches the high-low limit of the authors' earlier method. Upper bound only; the lower bound is unchanged.
events.remains: The lower bound (log n / n^2 is still the best recorded lower bound in the sources I read); the sharp order; the exponent between 7/6 and the earlier 8/7.

The paper's own Heilbronn section (Section 29) could not be read: the HTML fetch truncates before it and the PDF exceeds the fetch size limit. Figure values are therefore from search excerpts.

events.what_happened: Sudermann-Merx, 'Heilbronn's Problem in the Unit Triangle: Certified Optimal Configurations for up to n <= 8', arXiv:2607.15021 (v1 16 Jul 2026; v2 22 Jul 2026). Proves that for n >= 5, unless all three vertices of the unit right triangle are occupied, some optimal configuration has at least four points on the boundary (Proposition 1). Gives certified optima for n <= 8 by a mixed-integer model (Gurobi 13, MIP gap 10^-4, SymPy); claims the n = 8 optimality proof is 'to our knowledge the first'. Says the n = 8 optimum is a root of a septic polynomial conjectured by Chen, Zeng and Zhou, with Galois group S7. Acknowledges Erich Friedman for unpublished configurations.
events.delivers: Unit right triangle variant, finite n: certified optima for n <= 8 (n = 5, 6 previously proved by others; n = 7 Cantrell's, optimality earlier by Zeng and Chen; n = 8 claimed first proof). Not the unit square; not asymptotic.
events.remains: The unit triangle for n >= 9; the unit square; the simultaneous minimality of the eleven triangles in T11 (stated open in the paper).

The paper's abstract says 'certifies global optimality'; the referee reads this as an overstatement. One automated review only.

events.what_happened: Trela, 'KKT Stresses, Affine Moments, and Separator Flux in the Heilbronn Triangle Problem', arXiv:2609.25035 (24 Aug 2026, one version, 37 pages): stress theory for positive-area local optima of the unit-square max-min problem; shows the normalised KKT multipliers satisfy an equilibrium relation with the outward square reaction; every positive stress component meets all four sides and there are at most two such components; an exact interface-flux law; a Pfaffian result for a five-internal-vertex block; and, by analytic reduction plus exact symbolic enumeration, exclusion of every one-external completion of a specified one-silent five-cycle residual.
events.delivers: Unit square: structural constraints on local optima (stress and moment identities). No bound on the optimum. The author states these 'isolate the remaining degeneracy but do not solve the problem for arbitrary n'.
events.remains: The optimum for arbitrary n; the bounds; the degeneracy the paper leaves open.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was read; the symbolic enumeration's code and the claimed exclusion were not examined.
events.direction: Structural theory; no movement in the bound.

events.what_happened: Agama, arXiv:2006.05269 v12 (8 Mar 2026) and v13 (6 May 2026): for the UNIT DISC, adds the upper bound Delta(s) << 1 / s^(3/2 - eps) (eps depends on s and is small), alongside the lower bound Delta(s) >> log s / (s sqrt s). The abstract states the authors 'improve on the current upper and lower bounds' by 'ideas from the geometry of compression'. The v12 comments field says 'ideas remained unchanged but the paper has been reformatted' and records an administrative note of substantial text overlap with arXiv:1912.08075 and arXiv:2002.00502. Whether the upper bound first appeared in v12 rather than an earlier version was not checked.
events.revisions: v12 8 Mar 2026 (first version I confirmed carrying the upper bound); v13 6 May 2026.
events.delivers: Unit disc (container variant): claimed upper bound Delta(s) << s^(-3/2+eps). If correct, this is stronger than the n^(-7/6+o(1)) upper bound that the Erdos #507 page gives for the same disc problem. Not the unit square.
events.remains: The unit square; the sharp order.
events.doubts: The claimed upper bound would beat the Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov exponent for the disc variant, and no expert engagement was found. Earlier versions of the same paper carried a different lower-bound claim (see agama-2020 and agama-2024). The arXiv comment records text overlap with two other arXiv papers. No peer-reviewed version found.
events.direction: Upper-bound claim for the unit disc (container variant), which would lower the disc optimum further.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound' (openai/math repository, family 191, manuscript path dated 25 Sept 2026; the repository release of 722 manuscripts was on 6 Oct 2026). The Lean scope note (lean/docs/191.md) says the formalisation 'constructs an unbounded sequence of sizes n and point sets for which every triangle has area at least n^(-2+eta)' for one fixed eta > 0, and 'refutes the proposed upper bound of order n^(-2+epsilon) for every epsilon > 0'. The note adds that the paper's statement 'for every sufficiently large n' is broader than the linked construction. The Lean file lean/ComparatorChallenges/HeilbronnTriangle.lean (namespace Problem355) states theorem heilbronn_power_lower_bound (existence of P_j with n_j tending to infinity, each triangle area >= n_j^(-2+eta)) and theorem almost_n_minus_two_refuted (not eventually bounded by n^(-2+eta/2)). With eta defined as 1/(100000 (T^2+1)), T = C(C(163,41),3). Both theorems end in 'sorry' on the pinned commit adc7f12 and on main as read. The manuscript main.pdf could not be decoded, so the paper's abstract, main theorem and proof were not read.
events.revisions: Manuscript dated 25 Sept 2026 by its path; public in the openai/math release on 6 Oct 2026. history.md (last entry 7 Oct 2026) lists the three withdrawn manuscripts and 14 revised manuscripts, neither of which includes family 191; no later revision found.
events.delivers: Unit square (the Lean statement uses points in [0,1]^2). Lower bound: for an unbounded sequence of n, a configuration of n points whose minimum triangle area is at least n^(-2+eta), with eta > 0 fixed (tiny: eta = 1/(100000 (T^2+1))). This improves the unit-square lower bound from log n / n^2 to a power. As a claim it refutes Heilbronn's proposed upper bound of order n^(-2+epsilon) for all epsilon > 0. Per the Lean note, the paper's statement covers every sufficiently large n, which the Lean sequence does not. The formal statement is an existence claim; the manuscript's construction (explicit or not) was not read. The upper bound n^(-7/6+o(1)) is untouched.
events.remains: The sharp order of the unit-square optimum; the upper bound (still n^(-7/6+o(1)) in the sources I read); the paper's full 'every sufficiently large n' statement is not formalised.
events.directly_checkable: The Lean statements can be read directly; the construction in the manuscript was not read. The Lean existence statement gives no explicit point set in the file I read.
events.doubts: (1) The Lean file for this family contains 'sorry' in both theorems, both on the pinned commit and on main as read; I found no solution file among the 49 files visible in the ComparatorChallenges directory listing (the listing is partial). (2) The Lean statement covers an unbounded sequence of n; the manuscript's 'every sufficiently large n' is not formalised. (3) The manuscript PDF was unreadable to me, so the argument is unchecked. (4) OpenAI's own release disclosures: a spokesperson told Retraction Watch that roughly 50% of results were released unconfirmed, and that the advisory group recommended releasing results without waiting for full formalisation; three other manuscripts in the same release were withdrawn for a sign error. (5) The Blinov draft reports the pinned manuscript's packing exponent as about 3.18e-236, while the Lean eta as written is 1/(100000 (T^2+1)); I did not reconcile the two. (6) I found no mathematician's public comment specific to this family; the expert comments found concern the release as a whole.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction: a construction with minimum triangle area n^(-2+eta) in the unit square, larger than the log n / n^2 lower bound by a power. It is also a counterexample to Heilbronn's conjectured O(n^(-2)) bound (the problem statement itself asks for bounds, not that conjecture).
events.object: Per the Lean statement: for an unbounded sequence n_j of point counts, a set P_j of n_j points in the unit square whose every triangle has area at least n_j^(-2+eta), where eta = 1/(100000 (T^2+1)) and T = C(C(163,41),3). It is an existence statement; the manuscript's construction (explicit or not) was not read.
people: OpenAI (credited as the sole author on the manuscript)

events.what_happened: Ivan Blinov (GitHub littleBro), 'Conditional Heilbronn triangle bounds: finite packing proofs in Lean, exact certificates, and reproducible checks' (repository littleBro/heilbronn-triangle-bounds; undated; it pins the OpenAI manuscript at commit fd4aeeb and post-dates the 6 Oct 2026 release). Extends OpenAI family 191: a conditional exponent eta' = 1/(498 * 379^17 + 7), approximately 2.9235e-47, for Delta(n) >= c n^(-2+eta') for every sufficiently large n, conditional on the pinned manuscript's geometric estimates; dimension d = 13; centred-sphere packing with length-17 words over a 190-symbol alphabet, base-379 encoding, a central energy interval of 20,001 energies and T = C(C(51,13),3) words chosen from one layer without enumerating the sphere. The README says the second-moment bound, layer selection, finite packing and selected scale inequalities are proved in Lean; the slab cap has a written finite-field proof; the geometry and the full theorem are not formalised; 'no independent peer review, priority claim or OpenAI endorsement'.

events.doubts: Conditional on an unread manuscript's estimates; the slab cap is not Lean-proved; the README says novelty, optimality and independent mathematical review are not established. Not peer reviewed.

disputes.summary: The cached tejstead ledger dates the AlphaEvolve triangle n = 11 (0.03652) and convex n = 14 (0.02783) records to June 2025, while arXiv:2511.02864 has v1 on 3 Nov 2025. Either the constructions were public earlier (for example in the alphaevolve_results repository) or the ledger date is wrong. I could not confirm which. If June 2025 is right, the alphaevolve-2025 event moves earlier but stays in the window.

Unit square n = 22: the cached ledger gives 0.009569 (August 2026, Sudermann-Merx); the live table gives 0.01077165 (+0.93%, 11 Oct 2026, Sudermann-Merx). The two cannot both be right as stated (the implied gain would be about 12%, not 0.93%).

Convex n = 31 and 33 (and square n = 25): the English aggregator credits 'Opus 5.5'; the Spanish and Russian versions name Rob Gardiner, Alexandar Lackovic, and Marc-Emmanuel Coupvent des Graviers; the codrAlex README credits Alexandar Lackovic's code with Claude Opus 5.5 help; the renidrag PR credits Rob Gardiner. The identities of the GitHub handles (codrAlex, renidrag) with these names are inferred, not stated.

The Sudermann-Merx triangle paper claims 'to our knowledge the first' proof of the n = 8 optimum. The Pith AI referee says the step is a Gurobi run at 10^-4 MIP gap and 'not a proof'. One automated review against an author's claim; no human referee report found.

OpenAI's README says roughly 42% of top-line results are formalised in Lean and that 'the repository has ~42% top-line results formalized'; for family 191 the Lean file in the repository is a statement file with 'sorry' in both theorems. Whether the family is 'Lean-verified' depends on whether a solution file exists outside the listed directory.

The Agama paper's claims change between versions: v1 (2020) lower bound log^2 s / s^2 for the plane; v9 to v13 lower bound log s / (s sqrt s) for the unit disc; v12 and v13 add an upper bound 1/s^(3/2 - eps) for the disc. Ellmann's paper (withdrawn v3, 2017) moves from a convex-domain claim to a unit-circle construction (v4, 2022) with a formula in v12 (2025).

summary: Found: (1) The unit-square lower bound has been claimed improved by a power in OpenAI's family 191, 'A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound', dated 25 Sept 2026 and public in the openai/math release of 6 Oct 2026. The Lean scope note describes a Lean statement giving, for an unbounded sequence of n, n-point sets in the unit square with every triangle area at least n^(-2+eta), eta > 0 tiny, and says the paper's own claim is for every sufficiently large n, which is broader. The Lean file in the repository, however, has both theorems ending in 'sorry' on the pinned commit and on main; I found no solution file among the visible listing of 49 files. The manuscript PDF could not be decoded, so I did not read the paper's argument. The family is not among the three withdrawn manuscripts (all Hodge-related) and not among the 14 revised, per the history file's last entry of 7 Oct 2026. The README credits the whole batch to 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' and states that the vast majority of results used the same procedure; family 191 is not in the exceptions list, so the attribution for it is by inference. I found no mathematician's public comment specific to this result. (2) Ivan Blinov's undated draft, which post-dates the release, gives a conditional exponent of about 2.9e-47 for the same kind of bound, conditional on OpenAI's geometric estimates; its author discloses substantial Codex assistance. (3) The unit-square upper bound moved in the window by Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov (arXiv 11 Sept 2024; published Inventiones 240, 2025): n^(-7/6+o(1)). Their 2023 bound (n^(-8/7-1/2000)) predates the window. The Erdos #507 page (last updated 30 Dec 2025) and Wikipedia as fetched still give this as the current best upper bound, and the Wikipedia article, as fetched after its 3 Oct 2026 edit, does not mention the OpenAI result or any AI. (4) Variant containers, several with AI involvement: AlphaEvolve's Heilbronn constructions for the equilateral triangle (11 points) and unit-area convex regions (13 and 14 points), arXiv 2511.02864 (Nov 2025), where the paper reports no improvement for the unit square; Maldague-Wang-Zakharov's 3D cube bound n^(-2/3-c) (Oct 2025); Agama's unit-disc bounds (2020 to 2026), whose claims change between versions and have no expert engagement; Ellmann's withdrawn 2017 convex claim and 2022 unit-circle construction; Sudermann-Merx's unit-triangle certification for n <= 8 (July 2026), where the Pith AI referee disputes the 'first proof' claim. (5) Finite-n unit-square and variant records in September and October 2026 on a community leaderboard and in contributors' repositories. Several credit 'Claude Opus 5.5', 'Fable 5.1' or 'OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex', but these credits appear only on the site, in competitors' READMEs or in an aggregator; I could not reach the finders' own account for the square n = 36 record, and I did not list code-writing help in ai.systems. These finite-n records are single cases of the quantity, not asymptotic movements. Close calls: (a) whether family 191 counts, given the unread manuscript and the sorry-marked Lean file; (b) whether finite-n records count as moving a bound, under section 2.1 they are single cases of the quantity; (c) whether AlphaEvolve's variant constructions count when the problem is read as the unit-square problem; (d) whether Opus 5.5 and ChatGPT/Codex code help is AI involvement in the mathematics; (e) whether the AlphaEvolve Heilbronn results date to June 2025 (ledger) or November 2025 (arXiv). Heilbronn-specific expert commentary was not found for any post-2024 event except the 2023 Quanta digest, which is a press digest rather than a verification.
competing_reading: Read strictly, the only event that moved the unit-square quantities in the window is the Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov upper bound (refereed at Inventiones). The OpenAI family 191 claim is an unchecked lower-bound improvement whose formal statement is sorry-marked in the repository I read, and which no mathematician has publicly checked. Read generously, family 191 is a real power improvement of the unit-square lower bound released with a Lean construction; if a solution file exists elsewhere in the Comparator setup, it is the strongest machine-checked lower-bound event on the problem, and the 'sorry' lines are only challenge placeholders. Under a container-inclusive reading of 'the Heilbronn triangle problem', the AlphaEvolve constructions, the Agama and Ellmann disc and circle claims, the 3D bound, and the finite-n leaderboard records all count as events on the same family of quantities, and the AI-involved ones are numerous.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The main.pdf of openai/math preprint 191 (abstract, main theorem, 'every sufficiently large n' versus the unbounded sequence, and whether the construction is explicit), and any solution file or comparator result for lean/ComparatorChallenges/HeilbronnTriangle.lean (the full directory listing, which was only partly visible). (2) A named mathematician's public check of family 191, or a referee report. (3) Section 29 of arXiv:2511.02864 (or the notebook for the Heilbronn problem in google-deepmind/alphaevolve_results) to confirm the figure values, the previous bests and the first public date (June 2025 or November 2025). (4) The primary record for the square n = 36 entry and the finders' own description of how it was found, plus the raw HTML of the live table to confirm the n = 22 and n = 33 values. (5) The Fable 5.1 team's own account of the September 2026 records. (6) The date of the codrAlex and Blinov records. (7) The full text of the Cohen-Pohoata-Zakharov papers, to check their acknowledgements for AI disclosures; I read only abstracts for those.

No Heilbronn-specific expert commentary on family 191 found in two extended searches; general commentary on the 722-manuscript release (Alex Townsend, Andrew Sutherland, an Association for Human Mathematics statement) concerns the whole release, not Heilbronn.

The Pohoata 'sharp exponent for the minimal distance problem' paper (arXiv:2607.20422) was described in a search excerpt as stating a Heilbronn conjecture Delta_H(n) <= n^(-7/6-c); the opened abstract page does not mention Heilbronn, so that claim is not used.
